title: GLEAM4 Global Land Evaporation and Soil Moisture (0.1°, daily)
description: The Global Land Evaporation Amsterdam Model (GLEAM), fourth generation, estimates daily actual evaporation and its components (transpiration, interception loss, bare-soil evaporation, open-water evaporation, sublimation), potential evaporation, evaporative stress, root-zone and surface soil moisture and sensible heat flux on a 0.1° global grid. GLEAM4.3a (1980–2024) uses satellite and reanalysis inputs; GLEAM4.3b (2003–2024) is based on satellite data.
purpose: An independent, observation-driven estimate of actual evaporation and soil moisture for Algeria's water balance and agricultural drought analysis, complementary to model reanalyses (ERA5-Land) and to MODIS MOD16 and WaPOR.

license_notes: gleam.eu 'User policy': 'GLEAM4 datasets are freely available; GLEAM datasets can only be used for commercial purposes after internal approval'. The GLEAM4 data descriptor (Miralles et al. 2025) states the data are on a public SFTP server 'under a CC BY licence' without naming a version; this record follows the provider website, which adds the commercial-use condition. Registration (name, e-mail) is required to receive SFTP credentials.

GLEAM4: global land evaporation and soil moisture dataset at 0.1° resolution from 1980 to near present. Scientific Data, 12, 416. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04610-y

references.citation: Miralles, D. G., Bonte, O., Koppa, A., et al. (2025). GLEAM4: global land evaporation and soil moisture dataset at 0.1° resolution from 1980 to near present. Scientific Data, 12, 416.

Miralles, D. G., Holmes, T. R. H., de Jeu, R. A. M., Gash, J. H., Meesters, A. G. C. A., and Dolman, A. J. (2011). Global land-surface evaporation estimated from satellite-based observations. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences, 15, 453–469.

spatial_extent.description: Global land on a 0.1° latitude–longitude grid; Algeria must be subset from global files.

temporal_extent.description: GLEAM4.3a: 1 January 1980 – 31 December 2024; GLEAM4.3b: 2003–2024 per the website Datasets section (the website highlights also say 4.3b 'covers up to the end of 2025' — check the README on the server). Monthly and yearly aggregates are also provided. New releases have extended the record periodically (4.2 described in the 2025 paper covered 1980–2023).

processing: Potential evaporation is computed with Penman's equation (including aerodynamic demand, new in GLEAM4) and reduced to actual evaporation through an evaporative stress factor learned from eddy-covariance and sap-flow data (hybrid machine-learning; GLEAM4.3 replaced the deep neural network with an XGBoost implementation). A multi-layer soil water balance accounts for plant access to groundwater, and ESA CCI surface soil moisture is assimilated with a Newtonian nudging scheme. Inputs are resampled to 0.1° by bilinear interpolation.
validation: Miralles et al. (2025): validation against 473 eddy-covariance sites gives a median correlation of 0.73, root-mean-square error of 0.95 mm/day and Kling–Gupta efficiency of 0.49 (GLEAM4.2).
limitations: Download requires registration and SFTP access (port 2225), so it cannot be scripted anonymously.
Commercial use requires prior approval by the GLEAM team.
Few eddy-covariance sites exist in North Africa, so the learned stress function is weakly constrained for Algerian steppe, oases and desert; the validation statistics are global.
The GLEAM documentation reviewed here does not describe irrigation as a water input; if it is absent, evaporation over irrigated perimeters and oases may be underestimated.
Precipitation and radiation forcing errors in data-sparse regions propagate to all outputs; version changes (4.2 → 4.3) modify values, so record the version used.

algeria_notes: Useful for comparing evaporation estimates across the Tell, High Plateaux and oases, and for root-zone soil moisture in drought analysis. In the hyper-arid Sahara evaporation is close to zero and dominated by rare rain events, so relative anomalies there are noisy. Compare with MODIS MOD16, WaPOR v3 and ERA5-Land before drawing conclusions on irrigated areas.
